papers.title: Deep Injective Prior for Inverse Scattering
papers.abstract: In electromagnetic inverse scattering, the goal is to reconstruct object permittivity using scattered waves. While deep learning has shown promise as an alternative to iterative solvers, it is primarily used in supervised frameworks which are sensitive to distribution drift of the scattered fields, common in practice. Moreover, these methods typically provide a single estimate of the permittivity pattern, which may be inadequate or misleading due to noise and the ill-posedness of the problem. In this paper, we propose a data-driven framework for inverse scattering based on deep generative models. Our approach learns a low-dimensional manifold as a regularizer for recovering target permittivities. Unlike supervised methods that necessitate both scattered fields and target permittivities, our method only requires the target permittivities for training; it can then be used with any experimental setup. We also introduce a Bayesian framework for approximating the posterior distribution of the target permittivity, enabling multiple estimates and uncertainty quantification. Extensive experiments with synthetic and experimental data demonstrate that our framework outperforms traditional iterative solvers, particularly for strong scatterers, while achieving comparable reconstruction quality to state-of-the-art supervised learning methods like the U-Net.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文针对电磁逆散射问题，与用户关注的生物力学有限元代理模型无直接关联。
llm.why_not_core: No FEA surrogate formulation, no biomechanical context, no implant mechanics validation.

summary_zh.motivation: 电磁逆散射问题中，监督学习方法对分布漂移敏感且缺乏不确定性量化。
summary_zh.method: 提出基于深度生成模型的无监督框架，学习低维流形正则化并引入贝叶斯后验近似。
summary_zh.result: 在强散射体问题上优于传统迭代法，与U-Net等监督方法性能相当。
summary_zh.validation: 在合成与实测电磁散射数据上验证。

summary_en.motivation: Supervised deep learning for inverse scattering is sensitive to distribution shift and provides only point estimates without uncertainty quantification.
summary_en.method: An unsupervised deep generative prior framework that learns a low-dimensional manifold regularizer and a Bayesian posterior approximation for uncertainty.
summary_en.result: The method outperforms traditional iterative solvers on strong scatterers and achieves comparable quality to supervised U-Net.
summary_en.validation: Validated on synthetic and experimental electromagnetic scattering data.

papers.title: Design of a Haversian system-like gradient porous scaffold based on triply periodic minimal surfaces for promoting bone regeneration
papers.abstract: INTRODUCTION: The bone ingrowth depth in the porous scaffolds is greatly affected by the structural design, notably the pore size, pore geometry, and the pore distribution. To enhance the bone regeneration capability of scaffolds, the bionic design can be regarded as a potential solution. OBJECTIVES: We proposed a Haversian system-like gradient structure based on the triply periodic minimal surface architectures with pore size varying from the edge to the center. And its effects in promoting bone regeneration were evaluated in the study. METHODS: The gradient scaffold was designed using the triply periodic minimal surface architectures. The mechanical properties were analyzed by the finite element simulation and confirmed using the universal machine. The fluid characteristics were calculated by the computational fluid dynamics analysis. The bone regeneration process was simulated using a in silico computational model containing the main biological, physical, and chemical variation during the bone growth process. Finally, the in vitro and in vivo studies were carried out to verify the actual osteogenic effect. RESULTS: Compared to the uniform scaffold, the biomimetic gradient scaffold demonstrated better performance in stress conduction and reduced stress shielding effects. The fluid features were appropriate for cell migration and flow diffusion, and the permeability was in the same order of magnitude with the natural bone. The bone ingrowth simulation exhibited improved angiogenesis and bone regeneration. Higher expression of the osteogenesis-related genes, higher alkaline phosphatase activity, and increased mineralization could be observed on the gradient scaffold in the in vitro study. The 12-week in vivo study proved that the gradient scaffold had deeper bone inserting depth and a more stable bone-scaffold interface. CONCLUSION: The Haversian system-like gradient structure can effectively promote the bone regeneration. This structural design can be used as a new solution for the clinical application of prosthesis design.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文主要研究骨再生梯度多孔支架设计，而非髋关节植入物或股骨柄的应力遮挡分析。
llm.why_not_core: Does not quantify proximal femur stress/strain in Gruen zones, does not report micromotion with contact/friction modeling, and is not patient-specific or comparing intact vs implanted femur.

summary_zh.motivation: 通过仿生梯度结构提高多孔支架的骨再生能力
summary_zh.method: 基于三周期极小曲面设计类似哈弗系统的梯度支架，并进行有限元模拟和计算流体动力学分析
summary_zh.result: 梯度支架比均匀支架具有更好的应力传导和减少应力遮挡效果，体内外实验证明可促进骨再生
summary_zh.validation: 有限元模拟、机械测试、计算流体动力学、体外细胞实验和12周动物实验验证

summary_en.motivation: To improve bone regeneration capability of porous scaffolds by mimicking the Haversian system with a gradient pore structure.
summary_en.method: A gradient scaffold was designed using triply periodic minimal surface architectures, and its mechanical and fluid properties were analyzed via finite element simulation and computational fluid dynamics.
summary_en.result: The biomimetic gradient scaffold exhibited superior stress conduction, reduced stress shielding, and enhanced bone regeneration in both in vitro and in vivo studies.
summary_en.validation: Validation included mechanical testing, computational fluid dynamics, in vitro cell assays, and 12-week in vivo animal experiments.
